name: Kṛṣṇa
summary: Speaker of the Bhagavad Gītā. In chs. 4–6 he says he first taught the imperishable yoga to Vivasvat (4.1), that he has passed through many births which he knows (4.5), and that, though unborn and lord of beings, he comes into being by his own māyā age after age to protect the good and establish dharma (4.6–8); he is the enjoyer of sacrifices and austerities, great lord of all worlds and friend of all beings (5.29), and the one whom the most yoked yogin worships with faith (6.47).

name: Arjuna
summary: Addressee of the Bhagavad Gītā. In chs. 4–6 he is called Kṛṣṇa's devotee and friend (4.3); he asks how Kṛṣṇa could have taught Vivasvat (4.4), which is better, renunciation or the yoga of action (5.1), objects that the mind is too restless for the yoga of sameness (6.33–34), and asks the fate of one who falls from yoga (6.37–39).

name: Vivasvat
summary: Named in Bhagavad Gītā 4.1 as the first to receive the imperishable yoga from Kṛṣṇa, who told it to Manu; Arjuna objects that Vivasvat's birth was earlier than Kṛṣṇa's (4.4). The text does not further identify him (tradition: the Sun).

name: Manu (Vaivasvata)
summary: Bhagavad Gītā 4.1: Vivasvat told the yoga to Manu, and Manu told it to Ikṣvāku. The text says only 'Manu'; commentators identify him as Vivasvat's son.

name: Ikṣvāku
summary: Bhagavad Gītā 4.1: received the yoga from Manu; after him the royal sages knew it through succession until it was lost over time (4.2).
